prerequisites: Completion of Physics I and Physics II, and Chemical Fundamentals in Engineering from the first year is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling learning of new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Mechanical Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Know the structure, composition, processing, properties, and in-service behavior of different material families and their interrelationships.
Be able to select materials based on their applications in different fields of engineering.
Know the most appropriate standardized tests for evaluating material properties and behavior, and analyze and interpret the results.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Materials Science and Technology
Mechanical properties of materials. Plastic deformation mechanisms
Materials selection and design. Economic and environmental considerations. Materials recycling.
teaching_methods: Lectures (2 hours/week), full group, explaining basic topics using audiovisual aids.
Classroom practical sessions and seminars (2 hours every 2 weeks), medium groups, for exercises and theoretical-practical cases.
Laboratory practical sessions (2 hours/week for 7 sessions), small groups.
Tutorials (3h in-person + 1h virtual minimum per semester), individual or small groups.
Laboratory practice #6 (Corrosion) and practical case seminar conducted in English, including report submission.
AI-assisted writing (for text review and style improvement, with referencing).
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is the default, but students may opt for unique assessment. For continuous assessment, the final grade (CF) is calculated as 0.1*Personal Work + 0.1*Oral Presentation + 0.2*Laboratory Practicals + 0.6*Exams. A minimum of 5 must be obtained in each partial exam, and 80% of practicals must be completed with approved reports to pass; otherwise, the final grade is based on the weighted exam score or a fail (3.4) if practicals are not passed. Unique assessment, which applies to the second call and for students who opt out of continuous assessment, consists of a theoretical exam (80%) and a practical exam (20%). A minimum score of 5.0 is required in both exams to pass. Grades for practical laboratory work are retained for subsequent calls and academic years.
